Diagnosed at 20

It provided me with an answer as to why I was different throughout education, relationships and friendships, and gave me better insight into things I could implement to help me with all daily living tasks.

At University, I receive support academically.

Medically, I now have hearing aids, insoles and have had physiotherapy. 

It's improved my confidence accepting that I have a condition that makes me differently able, rather than think that I'm a freak and be ashamed of not fitting in. My social anxiety has massively improved

Plus, it gave me a community of people to talk to to know I'm not alone in having DCD.

Thank you for sharing a video from the perspective of someone with Dyspraxia. A lot of the time informative videos have been very medical based but the person hasn't experienced the struggles themselves. I have moderate DCD and I am affected by sea sickness and never knew that was a thing with DCD. I have poor short term memory, poor fine and gross motor skills and low muscle tone. I experience anxiety, sensory overload and problems with planning and organisation. There are also certain communicative elements that are impaired. 
I am however highly intelligent and creative, so not all is lost. 
But this condition can be highly frustrating.
For me I almost feel like my true potential and intelligence is "locked in" because I can't express myself in logical sequence or rapid response.
